newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas softens at front end, trade busy.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas softens at front end, trade busy.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures eased lower at the front end of the forward curve on Wednesday after two busy sessions which saw one deal "busted" or cancelled by the Exchange.
A total of 535 lots, or 535,000 therms a day, changed hands taking open interest to just over 5000 lots, or 5.16 million therms a day.
October was the busiest month, with 200 lots traded at weaker prices. The month settled 0.075 cents lower at 11.10 pence a therm (p/th).
September was the biggest faller, ending the day 0.20 p/th lower at 9.4 p/th.
In the morning session, a trade on September was cancelled by the IPE because it was a "manifest error".
A trade for 100 lots or 100,000 therms a day was done at 0.95 p/th after a seller erroneously inputted the offer at that price instead of at 9.50 p/th.
If the trade had not been busted the mistake would have cost the seller 256,500 stg.
An IPE spokeswoman said that the Exchange would cancel trades if a clear mistake is made in order "to ensure an orderly market".
But some market players said that busted trades harmed the Exchange's credibility.
Two orders placed in error on the screen-based trading system were cancelled on the second day of the contract in February.
The IPE will on Friday introduce a decimal point to screen prices which its says should help prevent such errors reoccurring.
Trades were also done in the first quarter and summer next year on Wednesday with the market moving in mixed directions.
